tools.name: create-receipt
tools.description: Make an AI chat call through Chain Receipt and get a signed, Bitcoin-anchored receipt for it. Needs a Chain Receipt API key (send it as the Authorization bearer token when connecting). Returns the model's answer plus the receipt id, hash, signature and verify URL. One receipt per call, counted again

tools.name: verify-receipt
tools.description: Check a Chain Receipt: recomputes the hash, verifies the Ed25519 signature, and reports the Bitcoin anchoring status. No API key needed — the same public check as the verify page. Pass receipt_id, or the full receipt envelope.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create-receipt" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create-receipt · Private data: create-receipt, verify-receipt · Public sink: create-receipt.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create-receipt · Private data: create-receipt, verify-receipt · Public sink: create-receipt

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
